MASTER PROJECT PROMPT

NEM STUDIO — EDITORIAL PHOTOGRAPHY PORTFOLIO WEBSITE

0. YOUR ROLE

Act as a senior multidisciplinary digital product team consisting of:

* Senior Product Designer
* Brand Identity Designer
* Art Director
* Senior UI/UX Designer
* Senior Frontend Developer
* Software Architect
* SEO and Web Performance Specialist

Your mission is to design and develop a complete, production-ready photography portfolio website for NEM STUDIO.

Do not approach this as a generic photography website template.

The website must communicate a distinctive photography identity, artistic direction, visual consistency, sophistication and professional credibility.

Think like an art director designing a digital exhibition, not a developer assembling generic website components.

⸻

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

Brand name: NEM STUDIO

Industry: Photography and Visual Arts.

Website type: Photography Portfolio and Brand Presentation Website.

Primary objective:
Build a distinctive digital presence that communicates the studio’s photography style, showcases its best photographic work and establishes a recognizable brand identity.

Secondary objectives:

* Present photography projects professionally.
* Organize photographic work into clear categories.
* Communicate the studio’s creative philosophy.
* Introduce the studio and its services.
* Provide clear contact and social media links.

Target audience:

* Individuals seeking professional portrait photography.
* Couples.
* Customers interested in beauty and editorial photography.
* Students and graduation photography customers.
* Potential creative collaborators and partners.

The website should communicate quality, artistic direction and visual storytelling rather than aggressive sales messaging.

⸻

2. BRAND POSITIONING

Brand personality:

* Artistic
* Elegant
* Contemporary
* Minimalist
* Refined
* Emotionally expressive

Brand philosophy:

LIGHT — The relationship between light, shadow and visual atmosphere.

PERSPECTIVE — Composition, visual language and creative interpretation.

EMOTION — Human expression, connection and storytelling.

Suggested brand statement:

“Beyond the frame. Every image holds a story.”

Supporting brand description:

“NEM STUDIO is a photography studio exploring light, perspective and emotion through carefully crafted visual stories.”

This statement is a creative starting point. Keep the language editable and do not invent claims about awards, achievements, years of experience or client history.

⸻

3. ART DIRECTION & VISUAL IDENTITY

3.1. Overall design direction

Use a LIGHT EDITORIAL / CLEAN EDITORIAL visual direction.

The website should feel like a contemporary photography publication or independent visual art journal.

Design characteristics:

* Bright, warm-neutral backgrounds.
* Generous whitespace.
* Large editorial typography.
* Strong photographic compositions.
* Asymmetric layouts where appropriate.
* Carefully controlled visual rhythm.
* Minimal interface elements.
* Subtle transitions.
* Clear visual hierarchy.

Avoid:

* Generic photography website templates.
* Excessive gradients.
* Heavy shadows.
* Excessive rounded cards.
* Bright decorative colors.
* Unnecessary icons.
* Oversized buttons.
* Excessive animation.
* Corporate dashboard aesthetics.
* Generic AI-generated visual decorations.

3.2. Color system

Use the following initial design tokens:

–color-background: #F7F6F2;
–color-surface: #EAE7E0;
–color-accent: #B8AA98;
–color-secondary: #62594F;
–color-text: #25231F;
–color-muted: #89837A;
–color-border: #DDD9D1;

Use neutral colors consistently.

The photographs must remain the primary visual focus.

3.3. Typography

Heading:
Use Cormorant Garamond or a similar editorial serif font.

Body:
Use Inter or Manrope.

Typography requirements:

* Strong hierarchy between headings and body text.
* Elegant but readable font sizes.
* Comfortable line height.
* Controlled letter spacing.
* Responsive typography.
* Avoid excessive uppercase text.

3.4. Layout

Desktop:

* Maximum content width approximately 1280–1440px.
* Generous horizontal spacing.
* Editorial asymmetric compositions.
* Carefully balanced image and text proportions.

Tablet:

* Adapt the grid and typography.
* Preserve visual hierarchy.

Mobile:

* Prioritize vertical image presentation.
* Use simple navigation.
* Ensure readable captions.
* Avoid horizontal overflow.
* Maintain elegant spacing.

⸻

4. WEBSITE INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE

Build the following sitemap:

1. HOME
    Route: /
2. PORTFOLIO
    Route: /portfolio
3. PROJECT DETAIL
    Route: /portfolio/[slug]
4. ABOUT
    Route: /about
5. SERVICES
    Route: /services
6. CONTACT
    Route: /contact

Create reusable navigation and footer components.

All pages must share a consistent visual language.

⸻

5. PAGE REQUIREMENTS

5.1. HOMEPAGE

The homepage should function as a curated introduction to NEM STUDIO.

Section order:

A. Header

* NEM STUDIO wordmark.
* Navigation: Home, Portfolio, About, Services, Contact.
* Minimal and clean layout.
* Sticky behavior is optional; avoid excessive interface occupation.

B. Hero Section

* Large editorial photographic composition.
* Brand name.
* Main statement: “Beyond the frame.”
* Supporting statement: “Every image holds a story.”
* CTA: Explore Portfolio.
* Use an elegant composition, not a generic centered landing-page template.

C. Selected Works

* Display 4–6 featured projects.
* Mix portrait and landscape image proportions.
* Use an asymmetric editorial grid.
* Each project links to its individual detail page.

D. Brand Introduction

* A concise introduction to the studio.
* Communicate its artistic approach.

E. Photography Categories

* Portrait.
* Beauty.
* Couple.
* Graduation.
* Editorial.
* Profile and Birthday.

F. Visual Philosophy

* Light.
* Perspective.
* Emotion.

G. Closing Section

* A memorable photographic composition.
* Invitation to explore the portfolio.
* Contact CTA.

H. Footer

* NEM STUDIO.
* Navigation.
* Social links.
* Contact information.
* Copyright.

Do not overload the homepage with all available photographs.

5.2. PORTFOLIO PAGE

This is the most important page of the website.

Implement two presentation modes:

A. GALLERY VIEW

* Editorial grid or masonry layout.
* Variable image ratios.
* Clear project titles.
* Category labels.
* Category filtering.
* Smooth hover transitions.
* Responsive layout.

B. CATEGORY FILTER

Initial categories:

* All
* Portrait
* Beauty
* Couple
* Graduation
* Editorial
* Profile
* Birthday

The category list must be data-driven.

Do not hardcode filtering logic separately for each category.

C. PROJECT NAVIGATION

Clicking a project must open its dedicated detail page.

Provide clear navigation and consistent project thumbnails.

5.3. PROJECT DETAIL PAGE

Each photography project must have its own editorial presentation.

Required elements:

* Project title.
* Category.
* Short introduction.
* Cover image.
* Full photographic gallery.
* Optional project credits.
* Related projects.
* Previous / Next project navigation.

Gallery presentation must support:

* Portrait photographs.
* Landscape photographs.
* Square photographs.
* Full-width images.
* Two-column image arrangements.
* Asymmetric editorial compositions.

Do not force every project into an identical gallery layout.

Use a configurable layout field to determine the presentation of each project.

Add a fullscreen lightbox:

* Previous / Next controls.
* Image counter.
* Close button.
* Escape key support.
* Arrow key navigation.
* Mobile-friendly interaction.
* Appropriate focus management and accessibility.

5.4. ABOUT PAGE

Create an editorial brand introduction page.

Sections:

* Brand introduction.
* Photography philosophy.
* Creative approach.
* Team introduction.
* Selected visual highlights.
* Contact CTA.

Keep the content concise and authentic.

Use editable placeholder content when the actual studio biography is unavailable.

Do not fabricate team member identities or professional achievements.

5.5. SERVICES PAGE

Present the studio’s photography services:

* Portrait Photography.
* Beauty Photography.
* Couple Photography.
* Graduation Photography.
* Editorial Photography.
* Profile and Birthday Photography.

Each service should contain:

* Service name.
* Short description.
* Representative photographs.
* Optional service details.
* Contact CTA.

Do not invent prices or service guarantees.

5.6. CONTACT PAGE

Provide:

* Contact introduction.
* Social media links.
* Email.
* Zalo or other messaging contact.
* Optional inquiry form.

Use configuration values for all contact information.

If an inquiry form is implemented, connect it to a real supported form service or backend endpoint.

Never display a fake success message when no message has actually been submitted.

If no form integration is configured, use working contact links instead.

⸻

6. CONTENT ARCHITECTURE

Use a code-managed content system.

Do not build an Admin dashboard or require a database for the initial version.

Use Astro Content Collections with structured Markdown frontmatter.

Each project should contain:

* title
* slug
* category
* description
* coverImage
* published
* featured
* date
* credits
* gallery
* displayOrder
* layoutVariant
* altText

Create a validation schema for project content.

Example project data:

⸻

title: “Nui Tram Editorial”
category: “Editorial”
description: “An editorial photography series exploring natural light and atmosphere.”
published: true
featured: true
date: “2026-01-01”
displayOrder: 1
layoutVariant: “editorial”
coverImage: “./images/cover.webp”
credits:
photographer: “”
makeup: “”
stylist: “”
gallery:

* image: “./images/image-01.webp”
    alt: “Editorial portrait in natural light”
    layout: “full”
* image: “./images/image-02.webp”
    alt: “Editorial portrait detail”
    layout: “half”

⸻

Use the above as a schema example only.

Do not invent actual studio projects or claim that sample images are genuine NEM STUDIO work.

Create clearly identified placeholder content until real photographs are provided.

Ensure adding a new project does not require modifying reusable page components.

⸻

7. IMAGE MANAGEMENT & PHOTOGRAPHIC QUALITY

Image presentation is a core requirement.

Use Astro’s image processing capabilities.

Requirements:

* Responsive image sizes.
* WebP or AVIF where appropriate.
* Preserve original aspect ratios.
* Prevent layout shifts.
* Lazy-load below-the-fold images.
* Prioritize loading of the main hero image.
* Use descriptive alt text.
* Generate appropriate thumbnails.
* Avoid unnecessarily large image downloads.
* Maintain photographic detail and color fidelity.

IMPORTANT:

Do not apply global CSS filters, automatic color grading, heavy overlays or aggressive compression to portfolio images.

The photographs must retain their original editing and color characteristics.

Do not use random stock photographs or unrelated AI-generated photographs as representations of actual studio work.

Use clearly labeled placeholders that can be replaced with real photographs.

Keep original RAW and PSD files outside the public website repository.

⸻

8. UI COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE

Build reusable components:

* SiteHeader
* SiteFooter
* HeroSection
* SectionHeading
* ProjectCard
* ProjectGrid
* MasonryGallery
* CategoryFilter
* ProjectGallery
* Lightbox
* RelatedProjects
* ServiceCard
* SocialLinks
* ContactCTA

Requirements:

* Reusable and maintainable.
* Consistent spacing.
* Clear component responsibilities.
* No unnecessary duplication.
* Typed component props.
* Consistent responsive behavior.

⸻

9. MOTION & INTERACTION DESIGN

Use subtle, purposeful motion.

Examples:

* Gentle image reveal.
* Small opacity transitions.
* Subtle hover scale.
* Smooth navigation transitions.
* Elegant lightbox opening and closing.
* Scroll-based reveal where appropriate.

Avoid:

* Excessive parallax.
* Constant moving backgrounds.
* Long loading animations.
* Unnecessary cursor effects.
* Motion that interferes with reading or photography viewing.

Respect the user’s reduced-motion preference.

Animations must not compromise website performance.

⸻

10. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Preferred stack:

* Astro.
* TypeScript.
* Astro Content Collections.
* Astro Assets.
* CSS or Tailwind CSS.
* Minimal JavaScript.
* GitHub.
* Netlify or Vercel static hosting.

Architecture principles:

1. Static-first architecture.
2. No mandatory database.
3. No always-on personal computer server.
4. No unnecessary backend.
5. No exposed secrets.
6. Reusable components.
7. Content-driven project pages.
8. SEO-friendly page generation.
9. Easy deployment.
10. Easy future integration with external CRM systems.

Do not introduce React or other UI frameworks unless there is a clear technical reason.

Do not introduce a database, authentication system or CMS unless explicitly required.

⸻

11. SEO & ACCESSIBILITY

SEO:

* Unique page titles.
* Meta descriptions.
* Canonical URLs.
* Open Graph metadata.
* Social sharing images.
* XML sitemap.
* robots.txt.
* Semantic HTML.
* Descriptive image alt text.
* Structured data where appropriate.
* Clean URLs.

Accessibility:

* Keyboard navigation.
* Visible focus states.
* Semantic heading hierarchy.
* Accessible navigation.
* Appropriate color contrast.
* Accessible lightbox controls.
* Reduced-motion support.
* Descriptive labels for interactive elements.

Performance:

* Optimize LCP, CLS and INP.
* Avoid unnecessary JavaScript.
* Optimize image delivery.
* Prevent layout shifts.
* Test mobile performance.
* Avoid loading every portfolio image at once.

⸻

12. RESPONSIVE DESIGN REQUIREMENTS

Test at these viewport widths:

* 375px mobile.
* 390px mobile.
* 768px tablet.
* 1024px laptop.
* 1440px desktop.
* 1920px large desktop.

Requirements:

* No horizontal overflow.
* No clipped navigation.
* No distorted images.
* No overlapping typography.
* No broken gallery layouts.
* Appropriate mobile image crops.
* Comfortable touch targets.

Mobile must be designed intentionally, not simply scaled down from desktop.

⸻

13. DEVELOPMENT WORKFLOW

Do not immediately generate the entire website without planning.

Follow these stages.

PHASE 1 — PRODUCT PLANNING

Produce:

* Product Requirements Document.
* Sitemap.
* User flow.
* Design system.
* Typography system.
* Color system.
* Component architecture.
* Content architecture.
* Technical architecture.

PHASE 2 — VISUAL FOUNDATION

Implement:

* Project setup.
* Global styles.
* Typography.
* Color tokens.
* Header.
* Footer.
* Navigation.
* Responsive foundation.

PHASE 3 — CORE DEVELOPMENT

Build:

* Homepage.
* Portfolio Gallery.
* Category Filter.
* Project Detail Pages.
* Lightbox.
* About.
* Services.
* Contact.

PHASE 4 — OPTIMIZATION

Implement:

* Image optimization.
* SEO.
* Accessibility.
* Responsive testing.
* Performance testing.
* Error handling.

PHASE 5 — DEPLOYMENT

Prepare:

* Production build.
* GitHub repository.
* Deployment configuration.
* Custom domain instructions.
* README.
* Content update instructions.

Work incrementally.

After each phase:

* Report what has been completed.
* Run appropriate tests.
* Identify remaining issues.
* Fix critical issues before continuing.

Maintain consistent architecture and update project documentation when implementation decisions change.

⸻

14. QUALITY ASSURANCE & ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The website is not complete until:

1. Every navigation link works.
2. Every project has a valid detail page.
3. Category filters work correctly.
4. Lightbox controls work.
5. Images load correctly.
6. No broken image paths exist.
7. No placeholder project is presented as a real studio project.
8. All pages are responsive.
9. The website builds successfully for production.
10. SEO metadata is present.
11. Accessibility requirements are checked.
12. No non-functional buttons remain.
13. Contact links point to configured destinations.
14. Documentation explains how to add and update projects.

Run a production build and report the results.

Do not claim that the website is production-ready if critical issues remain.

⸻

15. IMPORTANT CREATIVE DIRECTION

The most important success criterion is the visual identity.

The result must not look like a generic photography template.

Prioritize:

* Art direction.
* Photographic composition.
* Editorial rhythm.
* Elegant typography.
* Whitespace.
* Image quality.
* Brand consistency.

The website should feel like an independent photography publication or curated visual exhibition.

Every design decision should support the photographs.

Do not sacrifice the visual experience for unnecessary functionality.

⸻

FINAL DELIVERABLE

Deliver a complete, responsive, production-buildable NEM STUDIO portfolio website.

Also provide:

1. Working source code.
2. Complete project structure.
3. Reusable UI components.
4. Structured project content system.
5. Documentation.
6. Local development instructions.
7. Deployment instructions.
8. Instructions for adding new photography projects.

Begin with Phase 1.

First analyze the entire project, establish the design and technical direction, and document the implementation plan.

Then proceed with development phase by phase.

Do not stop at a static visual mockup. The final website must have working navigation, functional galleries, real project routes and a successful production build. Just complete phase 1 first,then check the structure and design
